## 1. Goal

Compute the measures every experiment and the website use (wait, turnaround, weighted completion, utilisation, makespan, per-priority wait) and write the state, results and metrics JSON exactly as PRD §5 shows. This settles O-4 (utilisation), O-5 (empty priority level) and O-6 (score for non-aging policies).

## 2. Background

**From PRD §5 JSON shapes:**

State, returned after every step:

```json
{ "ok": true, "data": {
  "now": 42, "done": 5, "total": 12,
  "cap":  { "cpu": 16, "mem": 32768 },
  "free": { "cpu": 4,  "mem": 8192 },
  "waiting": [ { "id": 7, "score": 6.200, "priority": 2, "arrival": 0,
                  "duration": 30, "cpu": 8, "mem": 20480 } ],
  "running": [ { "id": 3, "start": 30, "finish": 55, "cpu": 8, "mem": 4096 } ],
  "reservation": { "id": 7, "shadow_time": 55 }
} }
```

In the state, `reservation` is `null` when none is active. Event log entry:

```json
{ "seq": 17, "t": 42, "kind": "SKIP", "job": 7,
  "msg": "Job 7 skipped: needs 20480 MB, only 8192 MB free." }
```

Log kinds: `ARRIVE`, `START`, `SKIP`, `RESERVE`, `BACKFILL`, `FINISH`, `REJECT`, `BATCH_SELECT`, `PROMOTE_INFO`.

Metrics:

```json
{ "ok": true, "data": {
  "avg_wait": 12.4, "max_wait": 88, "avg_turnaround": 40.1,
  "weighted_completion": 5320, "makespan": 310,
  "util_cpu": 0.83, "util_mem": 0.71,
  "avg_wait_by_priority": [30.2, 28.0, 21.5, 18.0, 14.1, 11.0, 9.2, 6.3, 4.0, 2.1]
} }
```

**From BLUEPRINT §2 What we measure:**

**What we measure.** For each job: wait = start − arrival, turnaround = finish − arrival.

| Metric | What it tells us |
| --- | --- |
| Average wait | Overall responsiveness (primary goal) |
| Maximum wait | Starvation: the worst any job suffered |
| Average wait per priority level | Whether priorities are respected |
| Weighted completion time (sum of (priority + 1) × finish) | The Fan & Liang objective, for comparison with the paper |
| CPU and memory utilization | How busy the machine was |
| Makespan | When the last job finished |

**From DECISIONS D14, D17:**

| # | Decision | Reason | Rejected alternatives | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D14 | The live score S = b + alpha_milli·(now − r)/1000 is computed only when JSON is written, from integers, printed with exactly three decimals | Display only; never affects order; byte-identical output across platforms | Storing a floating score in the heap | R1 |
| D17 | Weights for weighted completion time and knapsack value are priority + 1 | Every job has positive weight 1–10, so priority-0 jobs still count | Weight = priority (zero weights); unweighted | BP §2, §3.6, R1 |

**From DECISIONS O-4, O-5, O-6:**

| # | Question | Why it matters | Decide in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| O-4 | Utilisation definition: busy resource-time / (capacity × makespan), and over which interval ([0, makespan] or [first arrival, makespan]) | Metrics JSON, E1 summaries | K-11 |
| O-5 | `avg_wait_by_priority` when a level has no jobs (proposed: `null`) | Metrics JSON, E3 summaries (`n_seeds` counts seeds where the level had jobs) | K-11 |
| O-6 | `score` in the state JSON for FCFS, priority and SJF | State JSON shape | K-11 |

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- Running totals updated O(1) per event (busy CPU-time and memory-time, sums of wait and turnaround)
- `sim_state_json`, `sim_results_json`, `sim_metrics_json` with the PRD §5 keys
- Live score for aging from integers, three decimals
- Deciding O-4, O-5, O-6 and updating PRD §5 first if a shape changes

**Out of scope:**

- Writing CSV files (CLI, K-12)
- `sim_log_json` (K-10)
- Reservation field contents (null until K-26)
- Python recomputation check (K-20)

## 5. Specification

```c
int  sim_state_json(const Sim *s, JsonBuf *out);
int  sim_results_json(const Sim *s, JsonBuf *out);
int  sim_metrics_json(const Sim *s, JsonBuf *out);
```

Definitions (BLUEPRINT §2): wait = start − arrival; turnaround = finish − arrival; weighted completion = Σ (priority + 1) × finish (D17); makespan = finish of the last job; average wait per priority level 0–9.

Live score (D14): for aging, S = priority + alpha_milli·(now − arrival)/1000, computed as integer thousandths `1000·priority + alpha_milli·(now − arrival)` and printed with `json_milli` (e.g. `6.200`).

Results JSON: an array of `{id, arrival, start, finish, wait, turnaround, priority, cpu, mem}` sorted by id (same columns as `results.csv`).

Averages (`avg_wait`, `avg_turnaround`, `util_cpu`, `util_mem`, `avg_wait_by_priority`) are not used for decisions; print them deterministically (e.g. fixed number of decimals from integer sums) so console and WebAssembly output stays byte-identical. Record the chosen format with O-4.

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** metrics are running sums updated at each event, so reporting is O(n) once at the end and O(1) per event during the run.
**Why weights priority + 1?** So priority-0 jobs still count in weighted completion (D17).
**Examiner question:** "How is utilisation defined?" — As decided in O-4: busy resource-time divided by capacity × the chosen interval.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Printing doubles with `%f` and getting different last digits on WebAssembly
- Integer overflow in Σ (priority+1)·finish (up to 10⁶ jobs × 10 × 10⁹ ≈ 10¹⁶, fits int64; check anyway)
- Dividing by zero when no job has finished
- Waiting list not in heap order in the state JSON
